1.why: Four full clauses with only one naming 'the inspectors' first signals a dangling-modifier item whose subject must follow the opening phrase.

2.why: Simple past is the unmarked default when the set offers one perfect, one present and one simple past.

3.why: 'Neither the coach nor the players' takes the nearer plural subject, so the only plural verb 'were' wins.

4.why: Only B has a matched pair of commas bracketing the supplementary 'in 1855'.

5.why: 'has hanged' is the execution sense and 'had hung' needs a past anchor; 'still hangs' is the idiomatic present.

6.why: Plural possessive is the only well-formed option; 'herds's' and 'herds own' are non-words.

7.why: Present tense 'shows' is the default for a standing finding, and the other three are each marked for a context not supplied.

8.why: Singular 'is' is the usual key when the set pairs one singular present against two plurals and a plural perfect.

9.why: After a semicolon a conjunctive adverb takes a following comma; B and D also add an illegal conjunction.

10.why: Singular 'it' is the only option that can refer to a single antecedent; 'they'/'those' are plural and 'one' is indefinite.

11.why: Parallelism with 'reading' and 'taking' forces the gerund 'asking'.

12.why: Only D puts the person 'Marcus' in subject position, which a dangling participial opener requires.

13.why: A plain compound needs no punctuation; the semicolon options both introduce a coordinator illegally.

14.why: The concessive relation needs a coordinating conjunction; 'however' and 'therefore' after a comma make comma splices.

15.why: The blank modifies 'the ancient scroll', so the passive participle 'Carefully unrolled by the archaeologist' is the only non-dangler.

16.why: 'Team' is singular, so possessive 'its'; 'it's' and 'there' are spelling traps.

17.why: Comma before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses; the semicolon-plus-conjunction options are redundant.

18.why: Singular past 'was' fits a completed historical subject; 'are' is plural and 'is'/'has been' are present-anchored.

19.why: The other three openers demand a human agent as subject, so the passive 'When examined' is the only safe modifier.

20.why: A finite singular verb is needed and 'is modeling' adds an unmotivated progressive.

21.why: 'its'' is not a word, 'it's' is a contraction, 'their' is plural; possessive 'its' remains.

22.why: Singular present 'anticipates' matches a singular subject where the set offers one plural and two marked tenses.

23.why: The only animate noun in the set, so it is the agent a preceding participial phrase needs.

24.why: 'the two species' migration routes' needs the plural possessive; 'specie's' and 'species's' are traps and 'species' is unpossessed.
